statusDetail: Complete atomic audit of the unauthenticated redirect/login surface. Protected post-login game routes were not entered because no credentials were supplied.

page.notes: The requested host redirects through five responses to id.gree.net. The representative accessible surface is the GREE authentication gateway.

artifacts.caption: Mobile layout metrics with zero overflow and CLS
Metadata, semantics, labels, and feature probe
Lighthouse performance, accessibility, best-practices, and SEO evidence

paths.description: Requested entry URL through its authentication redirect chain; represents the only unauthenticated archetype and core sign-in journey.
Submit the login form empty to inspect validation, error messaging, state, and recovery.
Post-authentication game routes were not covered because they require a valid GREE account; the audit does not fabricate credentials.

findings.evidence: The dark-emulated screenshot is pixel-identical to the light capture and the probe reports color-scheme: normal with a light rgb(241,242,243) body.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare light/dark support at the root and retint surfaces with system-aware color tokens.

findings.summary: Contrast preference does not change the presentation
findings.evidence: The prefers-contrast: more screenshot is visually identical to the default mobile capture, showing no preference-specific adaptation.
findings.suggestedFix: Use forced-colors-safe system colors and a prefers-contrast treatment for essential controls and links.

findings.evidence: The server-rendered login and registration/password-reset routes use ordinary full-document navigation with no view-transition declaration in the captured DOM.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a conservative cross-document View Transition for same-origin auth route changes, disabled under reduced motion.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visible on the two primary inputs
findings.evidence: The focus probe reports outline none and box-shadow none for both email and password inputs; several text links are only 16px tall.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible ring and enlarge compact link hit areas to at least 24 CSS px, preferably 44px for touch.

findings.summary: Redirect chain makes first paint very slow
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured FCP/LCP at 7.6s and the trace measured LCP at 4995ms. Five redirects add about 5.38s before the final login page.
findings.suggestedFix: Collapse the authentication redirect chain and send unauthenticated users directly to the canonical login endpoint.

findings.summary: Most of the page stylesheet is unused
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 15,156 bytes, 92.99%, of reg.css unused on this small login page.
findings.suggestedFix: Split critical login styles from the broad registration bundle and load only styles needed by this route.

findings.summary: Core authentication controls lack accessible names and labels
findings.evidence: Both visible inputs have no associated label. Lighthouse also identifies two icon-only provider buttons and one icon-only help link with no accessible name.
findings.suggestedFix: Add persistent label elements, accessible names for provider buttons/help link, and an accessible name/state for the password visibility control.

findings.summary: Important links and secondary action text fail WCAG contrast
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured ratios from 3.16:1 to 3.64:1 for password reset, help/contact links, and the app-login label, below 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken the blue and gray text tokens to meet 4.5:1 in every surface state.

findings.summary: The page has no main landmark
findings.evidence: The DOM probe finds header, footer, and nav but no main; Lighthouse fails landmark-one-main. Input focus styling is also absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap the authentication content in main and apply consistent :focus-visible styles.

findings.evidence: The viewport meta contains maximum-scale=1 and user-scalable=0; Lighthouse flags this as preventing low-vision users from magnifying content.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale and user-scalable restrictions, retaining width=device-width and initial-scale=1.

findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy on the audited entry response.
findings.suggestedFix: Set HSTS, a nonce/hash-based CSP including frame-ancestors, nosniff, strict referrer policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy across every redirect and final response.

findings.summary: Password-only authentication lacks a phishing-resistant option
findings.evidence: The login DOM exposes email/password and federated buttons but no WebAuthn/passkey capability; the page is an authentication surface where passkeys are relevant.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey sign-in and registration alongside account recovery, with password remaining as a fallback during migration.

findings.summary: Server errors are visible but not programmatically announced
findings.evidence: Empty submission returns clear Japanese errors, but the probe finds no role=alert messages and fields are not marked aria-invalid.
findings.suggestedFix: Associate each error with its field, toggle aria-invalid after submission, and announce the error summary through a live region.

findings.summary: Login fields omit labels and autocomplete tokens
findings.evidence: The visible email and password inputs have no labels and autocomplete is empty, preventing reliable password-manager and autofill assistance.
findings.suggestedFix: Use explicit labels and autocomplete=username and autocomplete=current-password.

findings.evidence: The final login document title is only “gree.net” and its description is only “GREE”, which does not identify the login task.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a task-specific Japanese title and description, such as “GREE ログイン”.

taskList.title: Make the login form accessible and autofill-friendly
